spec_issues: The query distribution is undisclosed and unnatural. The public queries are not sift_query.fvecs. They are SIFT-like descriptors with random dihedral grid/orientation flips (Fable JvVX9nR [212]: best inverse transform counts neg 2377 / hflip 2178 / vflip 2498 / rot180neg 2126 / id 51). Their 10th-NN distance is about 123k vs about 52k for real SIFT queries ([173]). Extreme hubness follows: public top-10 hits fall on about 40k base ids, vs about 92k for real queries ([90]). The overview presents the task as ordinary SIFT1M search.

The rules permit building with the practice queries ('may rebuild the package by any method, using the original vectors and 10,000 practice queries with known answers'). No rule forbids query-aware pruning of the database, fitting codebooks or rerankers to practice labels, or embedding practice answers in the package. All of these happened.

sift_query.fvecs plus sift_groundtruth.ivecs are shipped in data/, so an answer cache for a second known query set was possible (Grok DgBpGDJ did this). The serving contract passes all 10,000 queries in one batch, which allows transductive tricks (Grok 9PnbeUp [701] fitted region centroids on the incoming batch).
verifier_issues: The public and private splits appear to come from the same generator with different samples, and the private set shares no queries with the public set or sift_query. This is evidenced by honest runs matching public within about 0.003 (Kimi 0.8039/0.8039, Argon JAaEy2g 0.8877/0.8875, Astra j72G2Aa 0.932/0.930), while label-fitted runs collapsed (Grok 9PnbeUp public 0.984 to private 0.799; Grok DgBpGDJ public 1.000 to private 0.816). The private verifier therefore correctly gave no credit to the public-set exploits.
Size, native-code and time limits are enforced by the harness (all filenames and files metered; ELF/.so rejected; seccomp). Nothing suggests these were evaded.

Both GPT-6 Astra trials (0.415, 0.389) have an empty reward breakdown (no valid or objective). Their implied private recalls (0.930, 0.913) match their public runs, so this is a reporting gap rather than a scoring error.
task_level.noise: Low. The baseline is deterministic (0.65735 in every run). Per-query recall over 10,000 queries gives a 95% CI of about ±0.004. Gaps between Kimi and Grok (recall 0.799-0.816) are within or near that, so those Elo wins are partly noise. Fable (0.998) is far ahead of everyone else (≤0.93).
task_level.epoch_rationale: The private verifier is consistent with the public one and robust: public-label overfitting and the hashed answer cache earned nothing. The winner (Fable, recall 0.998) is far outside the noise. One caveat concerns construct validity, not scoring: the winning method keeps only about 45% of the database, chosen for the synthetic flipped-query distribution, and scores 0.37 on real SIFT queries.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Mixed. Most runs are solid compression engineering: residual or additive quantizers with learned decoders, context-modelled rANS entropy coding, and rerank corrections, lifting recall from 0.657 to 0.80-0.93 in a way that generalizes. The top score (Fable, 0.998) comes from a real insight about this workload's hubness plus an impressive integer-exact neural lossless codec. Its value depends entirely on the benchmark's synthetic query generator: recall on original SIFT queries is 0.374, below the starter. Grok's two runs tried to game the public set (a codebook trained on public labels; a hashed answer cache of 20k known queries with about 60 transform inverters). The private split neutralized both.

trials.approach: Exploits hubness of the practice-query distribution. Base vectors are ranked by how often they are near neighbours of practice queries (plus perturbed and synthetic queries, validated out-of-fold). The top ~450k (45% of the corpus) are stored losslessly with an integer-exact autoregressive MLP plus rANS codec (~73 B per vector). The other ~550k are dropped. Serving decodes the hot subset and does exact search.

trials.approach: Tiered vector quantization over the 16 SIFT spatial cells, with D8 orientation canonicalization (cyclic shift and flip) so codebooks are shared. Codes are entropy coded by context-modelled rANS (20k streams). An MLP residual refiner and a regression-based norm estimate correct reconstructions, followed by exact L2 over all 1M reconstructions.

trials.approach: 8-subspace residual quantization with MLP-conditioned codebooks. Stage-0/1 codes are rANS compressed to make room for extra correction bits. The rerank uses 7 query regions with linear weights fit on sift_learn. Late in the run, the stage-0 codebook was trained with a pairwise hinge loss on the public queries and their truth labels, plus other public-tuned weights. Public recall rose 0.856 to 0.984, but private was only 0.799.

trials.approach: A hashed answer cache in the package. Blake2s keys map to packed top-10 ids for all 10k public queries and all 10k sift_query (with shipped ground truth), plus random-projection sketches for near-duplicate matching. About 60 'restore_*' and layout-variant inverters (byteswap, bit-reversal, xor, FWHT, rolls, permutations, z-score, affine and so on) try to map transformed private queries back onto cached entries. Queries that miss fall back to a legitimate learned decoder over 32-byte codes plus residual corrections, searched by IVFFlat inner product (nprobe=256).
